name: Mitochondrial DNA Depletion Syndrome, Encephalomyopathic Form with Variable Craniofacial Anomalies
aliases: MTDPS Encephalomyopathic Form with Craniofacial Anomalies

criteria.description: Early onset encephalopathy with hypotonia and developmental delay
Presence of variable craniofacial dysmorphic features such as micrognathia, hypertelorism, and low-set ears
Identification of pathogenic mutations in genes associated with mitochondrial DNA depletion (e.g., FBXL4)
Biochemical evidence of mitochondrial dysfunction including elevated lactate in blood or CSF
Brain MRI showing cerebral atrophy and basal ganglia abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of early onset encephalopathy with craniofacial anomalies plus genetic confirmation of pathogenic mitochondrial DNA depletion mutations
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on genetic testing due to phenotypic variability.

searchTerms: progressive brain disease with skill loss
worsening brain function and developmental decline

pathognomonic.symptomName: Variable craniofacial dysmorphism including micrognathia and hypertelorism
searchTerms: facial differences like micrognathia and hypertelorism

common.notes: Detected via blood or CSF lactate elevation

laboratory: Reduced mitochondrial DNA copy number in muscle or fibroblasts
imaging: Brain MRI showing cerebral atrophy, basal ganglia signal abnormalities, and delayed myelination
genetic: Pathogenic variants in FBXL4 gene or other mitochondrial DNA maintenance genes
other: Muscle biopsy showing mitochondrial abnormalities including ragged-red fibers

distinguishingFeatures: Predominant muscle involvement without craniofacial anomalies
Later onset compared to encephalomyopathic form

redFlags: Rapidly progressive neurodevelopmental regression in infancy
Severe lactic acidosis refractory to treatment
Presence of craniofacial anomalies combined with encephalopathy
references: El-Hattab AW, Scaglia F. Mitochondrial DNA depletion syndromes: review and updates of genetic basis, manifestations, and therapeutic options. Neurotherapeutics. 2013;10(2):186-198.
Bonnen PE, Yarham JW, Besse A, et al. Mutations in FBXL4 cause mitochondrial encephalopathy and a disorder of mitochondrial DNA maintenance. Am J Hum Genet. 2013;93(3):471-481.
Orphanet: Mitochondrial DNA depletion syndrome, encephalomyopathic form with variable craniofacial anomalies (ORPHA:369897)
